library_preparation_preflight.summary: No new Maven dependency or Docker image is needed — every referenced class is already on the test classpath (jetty-security, which now hosts JAASLoginService, comes in transitively via jetty-ee10/ee11-servlet) and all 33 entries are pure in-JVM Jetty behavior. Meaningful gains come from richer test scenarios, not extra setup. Two entries are permanently unreachable on this repo's JDK 25 toolchain.
library_preparation_preflight.agent_guidance:
To raise coverage, extend JettyTests.java with scenarios that exercise paths the current tests skip — all achievable with existing dependencies:
- Add a real WEB-INF/web.xml descriptor (via WebAppContext.setDescriptor(...)) with <filter>, <filter-mapping>, <listener>, <context-param>, <session-config>, <mime-mapping>, <welcome-file-list>, <error-page>, <security-constraint>, and <login-config> elements to drive org.eclipse.jetty.ee10(/ee11).webapp.StandardDescriptorProcessor's visit* methods (the current tests register servlets purely programmatically, so the descriptor parser is never invoked).
- Register a ServletContextListener so ListenerHolder constructs IntrospectorCleaner.
- Enable HTTP sessions (SessionHandler / request.getSession(true)) to drive DefaultSessionIdManager's lazy SecureRandom construction (hits sun.security.provider.NativePRNG and SecureRandomParameters).
- Configure the Server's ThreadPool with a virtual-thread executor (e.g. QueuedThreadPool.setVirtualThreadsExecutor(VirtualThreads.getDefaultVirtualThreadsExecutor())) to hit Thread.isVirtual/Executors.newVirtualThreadPerTaskExecutor — stable on JDK 25, no preview flags or system properties required.
- Wrap the handler chain in org.eclipse.jetty.server.handler.StatisticsHandler to exercise SampleStatistic/Striped64 fields.
- Extend the forwardHeaders test with X-Forwarded-Proto, X-Forwarded-Server, an RFC 7239 'Forwarded:' header, and ssl-session-id/cipher-suite style forwarded headers to cover the remaining ForwardedRequestCustomizer$Forwarded.handle* methods.
- Configure a LoginService (e.g. HashLoginService with an inline test realm) plus a <security-constraint>/BASIC authenticator to exercise ConstraintSecurityHandler construction in both ee10 and ee11.
- Do not bother setting a SecurityManager system property: System.getSecurityManager()/checkPermission() in SecurityUtils are unreachable on JDK 25 regardless, since JEP 486 permanently disabled the SecurityManager.
risks: javax.security.auth.Subject.doAs(Subject, PrivilegedAction) and SecurityUtils.callableToPrivilegedAction (2 of the 33 entries) are only reached via SecurityUtils's pre-JDK-18 fallback path. On JDK 25, SecurityUtils.lookupCallAs() always resolves the modern Subject.callAs(Subject, Callable) handle first, so that fallback — and these two entries — can never execute. Realistic ceiling is 31/33 (~94%), not 100%.

The only Jetty code path invoking SecurityUtils.callAs/doPrivileged at all is SPNEGOLoginService (Kerberos/Negotiate auth); standing up Kerberos test infrastructure (embedded MiniKdc or a KDC Docker image) would still not reach the two dead entries above, so it is not worth the infrastructure cost for this issue.

org.eclipse.jetty.ee10.servlets.PushCacheFilter is a legacy HTTP/2 server-push mechanism now largely unsupported by browsers — verify with local Gradle/Native Image runs whether it's still reachable via ServletsConfiguration's default wiring before investing test-writing effort there.
